title: Teams Learn to Ignore Leaders Who Chase Fads
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This article describes a familiar leadership trap: enthusiastically launching a new idea after a book or podcast, only to abandon it weeks later for the next big thing. The author argues teams quickly learn to recognize this pattern and simply wait it out rather than engage seriously, which quietly erodes the leader's credibility over time. The recommended fix is for teams to respond to a leader's new enthusiasm by immediately building a concrete execution plan, which tends to hold faddish leaders accountable to actually seeing an idea through.
points: Leaders who repeatedly chase the newest idea from a book or podcast train their teams to disengage from anything new.
Team members learn to feign interest and wait out a leader's temporary enthusiasm rather than commit to it.
Each abandoned fad further erodes the leader's credibility, even when the underlying ideas have merit.
Building a concrete execution plan quickly can pressure a faddish leader into following through.
quotes: They tell everyone about the new insight and begin to rally support behind an idea or program that, if sustained, might add some value.

Leaders who follow fads usually don’t recognize how many times they have repeated the same pattern.
